title: p99/p95 tail latency deep dive with Orion Innovations
topics: KV cache effectiveness and cache hit patterns
summary: Redwood AE+SE ran a technical deep dive with Orion Innovations engineering to investigate observed p95/p99 tail latency on their production workload. Discussed streaming vs non-streaming behaviors, KV cache priming and hit-rate effects, batching tradeoffs for tail vs median latency, quantization options and quality impact, and network/VPC hops causing added jitter. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share benchmark spreadsheet, run targeted KV-cache priming test, provide quantization recommendations and sample kernels, and schedule pilot on a Dedicated node in Orion's VPC for a 2-week soak.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Mercer: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Alex from Redwood here, I'm the AE on the account. We'll run through the p95/p99 tail latency stuff you sent over. Jamie and Samir from our infra team are here.
[00:22] Priya Rao: Thanks, Alex. We've been hitting high p99 spikes during peak inference, some requests hit 1.2s when median is ~120ms so it's pretty bad for the chat UI.
[00:40] Jamie Chen: Ok, that's useful \u0002\u0004\u0008\u000c is that streaming or non-streaming traffic, or both?
[00:47] Priya Rao: Mostly non-streaming completions, but we do have streaming for shorter responses. The big spikes are on long-context renederings, the 8k context runs.
[01:10] Marcus Li: To add, about 30% of traffic is in our VPC to your Private deploy, rest via hosted API.
[01:28] Jamie Chen: Right, VPC adds a hop. Network RTTs matter for tail. Are those 1.2s p99s measured at app side or at Redwood's telemetry?
[01:40] Riley Barton: Our frontend measures them at the app edge. We see differences vs what you show in dashboards so trying to understand in-between hops.
[01:55] Samir Patel: Totally. A couple things to break down: model execution tail (KV cache misses, batching scheduling), network hops (VPC peering, NAT, proxy), and scheduler queuing during bursts.
[02:15] Priya Rao: Can we get into KV cache first? We're expecting high prefix reuse but may not be priming effectively.
[02:30] Jamie Chen: Sure. Our runtime uses a KV cache for autoregressive decoding; p95/p99 often map to cache miss patterns. If the request misses the KV cache we re-run earlier tokens which adds hundreds of ms.
[02:50] Devon Kim: Are cache misses common with long contexts? We thought once a conversation is hot it stays cached.
[03:04] Jamie Chen: Two common issues: cache eviction due to memory pressure and interleaved contexts. If your traffic mixes long and short sequences, the cache can get thrashed. Also note the default shard affinity on Dedicated influences hotness locality.
[03:27] Priya Rao: Makes sense. How do we measure hit rate in your telemetry?
[03:35] Samir Patel: We expose KV_cache_hit_rate per route in the Console; typical good numbers are >95% for chat workloads. If you're below ~90%, expect tail spikes. Also prefix cache (we call it prefix/KV) priming matters; initial few requests will be cold.
[03:58] Marcus Li: On our side, we see hit rates around 86-88% during bursts.
[04:06] Jamie Chen: There you go. That explains some p99. Two mitigations: tuned cache sizing/affinity on Dedicated, and proactive priming \u0002\u000f\u0010\u0013 you can pre-run the top N prefixes. We can provide a script to prime in your VPC.
[04:25] Riley Barton: Priming in our VPC \u0002\u0011\u0014 is that safe w.r.t. data? We need it to respect PII policies.
[04:34] Alex Mercer: Good call. We can prime with synthetic tokens or hashed prefixes, or run priming within your private cluster so data never leaves your VPC. We'll note options in the action items.
[04:48] Priya Rao: Next, batching. We tuned for throughput, but tails spike. What window should we target?
[04:58] Jamie Chen: Batching has a classic tail tradeoff. Larger windows improve throughput and median but widen tail. We usually optimize for two modes: low-latency mode (batching window ~5-10ms, smaller batch size) and cost-throughput mode (~20-50ms windows). For p99-sensitive UI, keep the batching window tight and enable continuous batching for idle fill.
[05:26] Devon Kim: Continuous batching \u0002\u0016\u0019 \u0002\u0017\u0018 that's Redwood's approach to avoid head-of-line waiting?
[05:33] Samir Patel: Yeah, continuous batching with micro-timeouts tries to fill batches without incurring big waits; but it needs predictable arrival patterns. Burstiness breaks it and causes scheduler queuing and jitter.
[05:49] Marcus Li: We do have unpredictable burstiness \u0002\u001a\u001d \u0002\u001b\u001c monthly reports and async agents cause spikes.
[05:56] Jamie Chen: For bursts, we recommend autoscale headroom on Dedicated and bursty queues with overflow to a cheaper model variant if latency SLOs are critical. Fallback routing keeps UI alive while slightly degrading output quality.
[06:12] Priya Rao: About quantization \u0002\u001e\u001f \u0002\u001d we saw some speedups with int8 but had quality regressions on our instruction-following tasks. Thoughts?
[06:23] Jamie Chen: Quantization is a quality vs latency story. int8 often gives 20-40% perf uplift with moderate quality impact; int4 can be much cheaper but may fail on some prompts. We provide quantization profiles per model and workload; we also ship custom kernels that reduce conversion overhead. We should run a small eval set you care about.
[06:44] Devon Kim: Can you share a sample matrix of int8 vs int4 errors vs throughput?
[06:50] Alex Mercer: Yes \u0002\u001f\u0007 we'll send the quant matrix and sample kernels. We'll also include the eval harness so you can run locally in your VPC.
[06:59] Riley Barton: Are quantized models compatible with KV cache? We worry about cache coherency/errors when mixing precisions.
[07:09] Jamie Chen: Good question. The runtime keeps KV cache per execution kernel variant. Mixing precisions requires a cache invalidation or separate cache namespaces. On Dedicated we can pin a kernel variant to avoid mixing; on Hosted we have automatic fallback but we'll need to coordinate to avoid mismatches.
[07:28] Marcus Li: Network hops \u0002\u0006\u0009 \u0002\u0005 can you explain where time is spent? We suspect VPC peering + edge proxy adding ~30-60ms.
[07:38] Samir Patel: At a high level: client -> app edge -> VPC peering + NAT -> Redwood front-door -> model runtime -> GPUs -> return path. Each hop adds RTTS and jitter. For VPC private deployments, we typically see ~10-30ms additional RTT depending on region and peering. Bad MTU or proxy timeouts can add more.
[07:58] Priya Rao: We traced a 120ms outlier to an L7 proxy dogtail yesterday.
[08:05] Jamie Chen: L7 proxies and TLS termination can cause blocking; keep TLS termination close to client or use mutual TLS to reduce handshakes. Also persistent connections and keepalives help.
[08:18] Devon Kim: Any logging we should enable to correlate traces end-to-end?
[08:24] Samir Patel: Enable request_id propagation and our trace hook; pass X-Request-ID and we'll show per-hop latencies in Console traces. We'll also send a sample agent config for OpenTelemetry.
[08:40] Priya Rao: Great. On measuring p95 vs p99, we have slightly different definitions between infra and product metrics \u0002\u0003 which do you recommend as single source of truth?
[08:51] Jamie Chen: Use the Console's end-to-end request measurement as primary: it records end-to-end time at the routing layer plus model execution. For app-side, keep it but correlate via request_id. For p99, include cold-starts and cache misses in the window, but have a separate "steady-state" metric excluding cold priming to track runtime behavior.
[09:12] Riley Barton: Can we see an example chart?
[09:16] Alex Mercer: I'll share a dashboard link after the call \u0002\u0001 sample dashboard with p50/p95/p99 and KV hit annotations. Link: https://redwood.example.com/dashboards/orion-p99-sample (placeholder).
[09:32] Priya Rao: About the pilot \u0002\u0008 we're interested in running Dedicated in our VPC. What does onboarding look like?
[09:40] Samir Patel: Typically we provision a Dedicated pool in your cloud account with VPC peering or PrivateLink; we push a small control-plane agent. For on-prem, we have an appliance-like package. We'll need network CIDRs, SSO details, and KMS integration for keys.
[10:00] Marcus Li: KMS \u0007 we use Vault. Does Redwood integrate?
[10:05] Jamie Chen: Yes, Vault via transit/CMK patterns is supported; we also support cloud KMS. We'll share the integration guide.
[10:14] Priya Rao: Security review required \u0002
 SOC2 + ISO?
[10:18] Alex Mercer: We have SOC2 and ISO attestation; we'll send the security packet link. For Private deployments, audit logs and HSM are options.
[10:30] Devon Kim: Back to latency: any kernel or model-level knobs we should tune?
[10:36] Jamie Chen: A few: 1) KV cache shard affinity (pin prefixes to GPU shards), 2) kernel selection (favor fused attention kernels for long contexts), 3) static vs dynamic batching thresholds \u0002\u000b prefer dynamic for variable lengths, 4) sequence chunking for very long contexts to reduce recompute.
[10:58] Priya Rao: Can you explain shard affinity more?
[11:03] Samir Patel: Shard affinity keeps related caches colocated on the same GPU or instance to avoid remote KV fetches. If your workload's conversation threads hop between shards, you pay cross-shard transfer. On Dedicated we can configure affinity rules.
[11:22] Riley Barton: Do cross-shard transfers show up in traces?
[11:25] Jamie Chen: Yes, you'll see a sudden jump in model execution time and a note in the trace when remote KV fetch occurs. We annotate these as remote_kv_fetch events.
[11:37] Marcus Li: How about streaming vs non-streaming? We saw lower tails when enabling streaming even though total time was similar.
[11:47] Jamie Chen: Streaming reduces perceived tail because partial tokens are pushed as soon as available; it can mask the p99 of final token generation. However, it doesn't reduce total GPU time; it can improve UX latency. For strict p99 UI SLOs on final answer you still care about backend tail.
[12:08] Priya Rao: Is it safe to combine streaming with quantized kernels?
[12:14] Jamie Chen: Yes, with correct kernel pipeline. Ensure the stream flush and finishing signals align; we have tested int8 streaming pipelines for many models. We'll include tests in the sample harness.
[12:27] Devon Kim: We heard about prefix/KV caching with ephemeral keys for multi-tenant; how does that work?
[12:34] Samir Patel: We namespace caches per customer and optionally per route; ephemeral keys can be rotated. For multi-tenant on a shared pool we enforce strict namespace isolation. On Dedicated you get complete memory isolation.
[12:50] Priya Rao: Actionable \u0002\u0004 what's the minimal experiment to isolate driver of p99?
[12:56] Jamie Chen: I'd propose three tests: 1) Priming test \u0002\u0005 measure p99 before and after priming top 100 prefixes; 2) No-batching test \u0002\u0006 force small batching window for a subset of traffic to see delta; 3) Kernel variant test \u0002\u0007 run int8 vs fp16 on identical workload. Each test should run for 30-60 minutes during representative traffic.
[13:20] Marcus Li: Sounds good. How do we route only a subset of traffic for tests?
[13:26] Samir Patel: Use route tags in Console and weight-based routing; we can split 10%/90% and gather metrics. We'll provide runbooks.
[13:36] Riley Barton: About cost \u0009 how much will Dedicated and kernel tuning cost us vs hosted?
[13:42] Alex Mercer: Dedicated is commit-based. Tuning/quantization often reduces token cost even on same cluster. We'll provide a cost comparison spreadsheet tailored to your throughput numbers.
[13:54] Priya Rao: Any gotchas for on-prem? We may test an air-gapped environment next quarter.
[14:00] Jamie Chen: On-prem has network isolation benefits but watch for GPU driver versions and kernel compatibility. We'll supply a preflight checklist for the appliance. Also quantized kernels may need specific CUDA/rocm patches.
[14:19] Devon Kim: Ok, let's talk next steps and owners.
[14:23] Alex Mercer: I'll recap and assign items.
[14:25] Alex Mercer: Action items: send benchmark spreadsheet, quant matrix, priming script, dashboard link, preflight for on-prem, sample OpenTelemetry config. We'll also schedule Dedicated pilot kickoff.
[14:38] Priya Rao: Can we get the pilot started next week?
[14:41] Samir Patel: We can aim for provisioning next Tuesday pending network details.
[14:47] Marcus Li: We'll send CIDRs and SSO info by Monday.
[14:50] Riley Barton: We'll run the priming script in staging VPC first.
[14:55] Alex Mercer: Great. Anything else?
[15:00] Priya Rao: One more question on telemetry retention \u0002
 how long do you store traces?
[15:05] Samir Patel: Default 30 days; extended retention is an add-on. We'll include retention options in the packet.
[15:13] Devon Kim: Thanks, this was super helpful.
[15:16] Alex Mercer: Thanks everyone \u0002\u000b we'll follow up with docs and schedule.
[15:22] (end)

Samir - provide priming script and OpenTelemetry sample config (2027-08-12)
